tagline: One of Latin America's largest metros, strung along the Pacific on the Costa Verde cliffs, with the port of Callao and its wildlife islands just offshore.
summary: Lima runs for tens of kilometres along the Pacific, its districts stacked on the Costa Verde cliffs above a single congested coast road. Alongside it sits Callao, Peru's principal port, with the yacht harbour at La Punta and, just offshore, Isla San Lorenzo — the country's largest island — and the Palomino Islands sea-lion colony. Millions move daily along the coast on the road network, while the bay itself carries only tour launches and port traffic, leaving the water under-used for passenger transport.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Ideal for the sheltered Lima Bay hops — Costa Verde to Callao (~9nm), La Punta to San Lorenzo (~4nm) and Callao to the Palominos (~8nm) — all inside Pioneer range, where morning-calm Humboldt-current water and short legs favour a fast, quiet, zero-wake craft.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for the ~112nm coastal express south to Paracas, beyond Pioneer range, where range and open-coast running matter more than turn frequency.

signature_routes: Costa Verde (Miraflores) ↔ Callao / La Punta — Lima Bay waterfront run
La Punta ↔ Isla San Lorenzo — sheltered island hop
Callao ↔ Palomino Islands — sea-lion wildlife express
Lima ↔ Paracas — Pacific coastal express (long-range roadmap)
transit_planning: Peru's transport investment has centred on the Lima metro, road corridors and the Callao port; scheduled passenger water transport on the bay is undeveloped, leaving room for an app-bookable tier alongside the coast road.

competitive_landscape: Lima Bay carries tour launches and port traffic but no scheduled fast passenger-vessel network; the coast is road-served and the islands are tour-served, leaving open room for a clean foiling tier with no direct incumbent on the bay.
seasonality: The Humboldt current keeps Lima's sea cool and often calm in the morning, with a grey coastal winter (roughly May-October); sheltered bay legs support year-round operation, while the exposed coastal express is best day-windowed.
regulatory_note: Maritime and port matters fall under Peru's maritime authority (DICAPI) and the Callao port authority; passenger-vessel licensing and bay navigation rules would frame any scheduled service.

precedents.why_it_matters: Shows durable leisure demand on the bay a scheduled clean craft can upgrade.
The user base already summons mobility by app, easing adoption of a booked water tier.
